results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I built a Sultai (blue-black-green) self-mill reanimator deck around a four-mana mass reanimation trick. No published list plays these three cards together, so this is an untested brew.

**How it wins:** Bringer of the Last Gift's enter trigger only works "if you cast it." Superior Spider-Man is cast and enters as a copy of any creature card in a graveyard, so he copies Bringer and the trigger still fires. For 4 mana instead of 8, every other creature gets sacrificed, then every creature card already in a graveyard comes back.

- **Turn 2:** Town Greeter mills four cards and keeps a land.
- **Turn 3:** Cast Overlord of the Balemurk for its 2-mana delayed (impending) cost. It mills four more and can return a milled Spider-Man to your hand.
- **Turn 4:** Spider-Man enters as a copy of Bringer.
  - Your milled creature cards come back.
  - Extra Bringers return as 6/6 fliers. Rune-Scarred Demon returns and searches your library for any card.
  - Overlords on delayed casting aren't creatures yet, so they survive the sweep.
  - If Ardyn, the Usurper was milled, he comes back and gives every Demon haste, lifelink and menace. Spider-Man counts as a Demon while copying Bringer, so your fliers attack an empty board the same turn.

Bitter Triumph and Winternight Stories let you discard a Bringer you drew. Late in the game you can also cast Bringer normally.

**Three directions I considered:**
1. Sultai self-mill, using the mill package from the Golgari Roots deck (Molt Tender, Overlord, Dredger's Insight, Cache Grab).
2. Dimir (blue-black) discard and card draw with Kaito and Winternight Stories. Green-only Town Greeter didn't fit.
3. Sultai ramp that casts Bringer for its full 8 mana.

I chose the first because it fills the graveyard fastest for the cheap Spider-Man line, and each card in it is either a creature that comes back or a way to get Spider-Man into your hand.

**Odds and risks:**
- You draw Spider-Man naturally by turn 4 only about 53% of the time. Overlord, Dredger's Insight and Cache Grab can each pull a milled copy back, so the real chance is higher.
- The deck checker reported a 0% chance of drawing every card in the win line by turn 5. That number expects you to draw Ardyn and the Demons, but they're meant to be milled, so it understates the deck.
- Bringer also returns your opponent's dead creatures. Against Izzet Aggro, time the sweep for when your graveyard is clearly bigger than theirs. The sideboard's Scavenging Ooze can exile their creature cards first.
- The mana base comes from Golgari Roots lists, stretched to three colors. It uses 22 lands; real Golgari Roots lists average about 21.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
I built **Temur Harmonizer Landfall**, a brew. Mightform Harmonizer doubles a creature's power every time one of your lands enters, so the deck plays lots of extra lands. Full Bore adds +3 power before the doubling starts, and Spell Snare (1 mana) stops the 2-mana answers this field uses against that turn: Get Lost, Shoot the Sheriff, Lightning Strike, No More Lies and Floodpits Drowner.

**Example kill on turn 4:**
1. Turn 1: Llanowar Elves.
2. Turn 2: Tifa Lockhart.
3. Turn 3: cast Harmonizer for its full cost (three lands plus the Elves).
4. Turn 4: sacrifice Escape Tunnel to make Tifa unblockable while her power is still 1.
5. Full Bore makes her power 4.
6. Play Fabled Passage. Tifa's own trigger and Harmonizer's trigger take her to 16. Crack the Passage and the basic it fetches takes her to 64.

The fast line has other routes:
- **Warp:** cast Harmonizer or Germinating Wurm cheaply with warp, then Full Bore. That also gives trample and haste, so it hits right away, and a land drop doubles it from there.
- **Traveling Chocobo:** it makes each land trigger an extra time, so one land drop doubles twice.

**Three directions I considered:**
1. A Boros-style Full Bore aggro deck. That's the only place Full Bore actually shows up, but it can't cast Harmonizer or Spell Snare.
2. Izzet Aggro's burn spells with a green splash. That gives few land triggers.
3. **Chosen:** the Landfall shell from the menu (Elves, Fabled Passage, Escape Tunnel, Tifa, Traveling Chocobo, Icetill Explorer), splashing blue and red. No deck has played all three cards together, and this is the shell that makes the most lands enter, which is what Harmonizer needs to do anything.

**Honest odds:**
- Drawing all six cards of that exact turn-4 line is rare (0.5% in the checker's simulation). It's a demonstration, and many cards can fill each role.
- More realistic: by turn 4 on the draw you see Harmonizer and Full Bore 25% of the time (with any of the 9 bodies worth doubling: Tifa, Hydra or Wurm).
- Harmonizer alone shows up 57% of the time. When Full Bore is missing, Harmonizer still turns any land drop into a big hit.

**Mana:** 24 lands. The deck has 22 green sources against about 26 in real Landfall lists. I gave up those few so I could have 13 blue and 13 red sources (counting the 7 lands that fetch basics) for single-pip Spell Snare and Full Bore.

**Sideboard:** aimed at the aggro decks (Abrade, Magebane Lizard), Cauldron and Reanimator (Soul-Guide Lantern, Seedship Impact), and Dimir and control decks (Spell Pierce, Repulsive Mutation, Surrak).

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Airbender Ascension, Bramble Familiar and Appa, Steadfast Guardian.
results.text:
I built this as a **Bant (green-white-blue) Airbending combo** brew for Standard. Its main win is a free loop between Appa and Aang. Airbender Ascension and Bramble Familiar are the engine and the ramp around it.

**How it wins**
- **The loop:** With Doc Aurlock out, spells you cast from exile cost {2} less. Airbent cards can be cast from exile for {2}, so they become free.
  1. Appa, Steadfast Guardian enters and airbends Aang, Swift Savior.
  2. You recast Aang for free. Because you cast a spell from exile, Appa makes a 1/1 Ally token.
  3. Aang enters and airbends Appa. Appa has flash, so you recast it for free and it airbends Aang again.
  - This repeats forever, making as many tokens as you want at instant speed.
- **The finish:** With Haru, Hidden Talent out, every Ally that enters (Appa, Aang and each token) turns a land into a creature with haste and adds a +1/+1 counter to it. That gives you huge hasty land creatures in the same main phase. Without Haru, you swing with all the tokens next turn. Aang, the Last Airbender is a slower backup for the loop; it isn't fast enough to answer things on the opponent's turn.

**What your three cards do**
- **Bramble Familiar:** a mana creature that, with Llanowar Elves, puts Appa or Aang down on turn 3. Its adventure half, Fetch Quest, is a late-game way to dig for missing pieces.
- **Airbender Ascension:** gets a counter each time a creature enters (mana creatures, tokens, recast creatures). Once it has four counters, it re-enters Appa at your end step, and Appa airbends your board again. With Doc out, recasting everything is free and each recast makes a token, so you get a strong engine even without Aang.
- **Appa:** the centerpiece. It holds up at instant speed with flash and makes a token every time you cast from exile.

**Directions I considered**
1. Selesnya (green-white) Allies with Earth King's Lieutenant and South Pole Voyager. This was fair and grindy, but nothing made airbending cheap.
2. Appa added to the Selesnya Offense shell from the meta. This was strong on its own, but it ignored Ascension.
3. **Bant with Doc Aurlock and Aang (chosen).** It turns your three cards into a real infinite combo. It's also how the one real list that ran all three cards was built. I borrowed the mana base and the Llanowar Elves package from Simic Ouroboroid.

**The honest numbers**
- **Combo odds:** You'll have Doc, Appa and an Aang together by turn 5 on the draw only about **25%** of the time. Most games you'll play a fair game first: tempo from airbending, 3 Get Lost and 2 Airbender's Reversal against aggro, and value from Ascension.
- **Thin colors:** The deck has 13 white, 11 blue and 16 green sources. That's thinner than Simic Ouroboroid, which runs about 14 blue and 21 green, because three colors share 21 lands. Great Divide Guide and the mana creatures help cover the gap.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Abandon Attachments, Firebending Lesson and Combustion Technique.
results.text:

**The plan:** Play cheap creatures on turns 1 and 2, then use the three Lessons to clear blockers. The plan relies on firebending, which adds red mana when a creature attacks; that mana lasts until the end of combat. Fire Nation Cadets gets firebending 2 (adds RR) once any Lesson is in your graveyard. Firebending Student adds red mana equal to its power, and it gets +1/+1 each time you cast a Lesson. That attack mana pays for Abandon Attachments and Combustion Technique in the middle of combat. The deck aims to win around turn 5, finishing with Burst Lightning or Hired Claw damage.

**What each requested card does here:**
- **Firebending Lesson:** For R, it deals 2 damage to a blocker. It's usually the first Lesson in your graveyard, which turns on the Cadets' firebending.
- **Abandon Attachments:** You discard an extra land or a spare Lesson and draw two. It goes to the graveyard as a Lesson, so it also grows Combustion Technique, and you can cast it with attack mana.
- **Combustion Technique:** It deals 2 damage plus 1 for each Lesson in your graveyard, and the creature is exiled instead of dying. There are 14 Lessons in the deck, so it should usually deal 4–5 damage by midgame.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Izzet Lessons tempo:** Sokka, First-Time Flyer, Dragonfly Swarm and blue Lessons.
2. **Ran and Shaw Lessons midrange:** Bigger and slower, built around dragon payoffs.
3. **Red aggro (my pick):** It uses the cheap creatures from Izzet Aggro (12% of the field), Hired Claw, Burnout Bashtronaut and Razorkin Needlehead, plus the creatures that care about Lessons.

I chose the third because all three requested cards are cheap red instants. The attack mana is what pays for them mid-combat, and dropping blue keeps the mana base fully red. Abandon Attachments costs {1}{U/R}, so it can be paid with red alone.

**Things to know:**

The checker reports almost 0% for drawing every card in my sample line by turn 5. That's because it names seven specific cards; the deck has several copies of each role.
- **Fewer lands:** I run 21 lands, compared with about 24 in typical Izzet Aggro lists. Every card costs 1 or 2 mana (1.49 on average), and the only Mono-Red Lessons list in the results ran 20.
- **One Inti:** I kept a single copy even though the checker noted few decks play it. Each Abandon Attachments discard lets it give you an extra card to play. It also lets you discard a Lesson when you attack, which grows Combustion Technique.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:

Its cast trigger sends every non-Elemental creature back to its owner's hand while all of yours stay. Bounce Off then returns Sunderflock to your hand for {U} so you can recast it and clear the board again the next turn.

**The three directions I considered:**
1. **Incarnation reanimator shell:** Deceit and Superior Spider-Man, with Ashling added on top. Real Sunderflock lists do look like this, but it would be four colours and ignores Ashling's red/blue flip.
2. **Izzet Aggro's Fear of Missing Out / Frostcliff Siege package with Ashling:** Sunderflock would just be a clunky 9-drop in an aggro deck.
3. **Izzet Elemental ramp (chosen):** It's the only one where all three cards do their real jobs:
   - **Ashling:** her flipped side, Rimebound, adds two mana each turn for spells costing 4 or more.
   - **Sunderflock:** its discount comes from your biggest Elemental.
   - **Bounce Off:** it lets you recast Sunderflock and repeat the board-wide bounce.

**What each requested card does here:**
- **Ashling, Rekindled:** Play her on turn 2 and swap a card for a new one when she enters. On turn 3, pay {U} to flip her for two mana right away, then two more every turn after. That mana works on Deceit, Mouth, Ice Flan, Twinflame Travelers and Sunderflock.
- **Sunderflock:** Your finisher. It also beats the two biggest decks right now, Landfall and Simic Ouroboroid, since neither plays Elementals.
- **Bounce Off:** Cheap tempo early. Late, it rebuys Sunderflock.

**The rest of the deck:**
- **Supporting cards:** Flamebraider gives two more mana for Elemental spells, in any colours. Twinflame Travelers makes Elemental triggers happen twice, so Rimebound makes four mana and Deceit bounces two things. Eclipsed Flamekin digs for Elementals or lands.
- **Removal:** Burst Lightning and Torch the Tower.
- **Mana:** The lands come from Izzet Aggro.

**Odds and caveats:**
- You have Ashling or Flamebraider by turn 2 in about 71% of games, and by turn 5 in 82%. You draw a Sunderflock by turn 5 in about 57% of games, not counting Flamekin digging or Ashling swapping cards.
- The checker says you'll have every card in my listed win line by turn 6 in only 1.6% of games. That's misleading: Deceit and Mouth are alternatives, so you only need one of them, and the line doesn't need every piece.
- It's an untested brew. The supporting cards (Flamebraider, Twinflame Travelers, Mouth of the Storm, Ice Flan, Eclipsed Flamekin) don't show up in any recent tournament lists.
- **Lands:** I run 23, a bit under the checker's suggested 24.5. Eight ramp creatures and two Ice Flans (which can trade in for an Island for {2}) make up the difference.

- **The "Rogue" shell:** The checker's suggested shell was a mislabeled Aang Allies list, so I didn't use it.

The sideboard is counterspells for Jeskai Control and Lessons, Abrade and Pyroclasm for Izzet and Boros aggro, Soul-Guide Lantern for Reanimator, and Sunspine Lynx.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Insatiable Avarice, Doomsday Excruciator and Archenemy's Charm.
results.text:

**The plan:** Bloodletter of Aclazotz makes the opponent lose twice as much life on your turn. That turns Insatiable Avarice's "draw three, lose 3" mode into a 3-mana spell that costs them 6 life. With all modes paid (5 mana), Avarice also puts Doomsday Excruciator on top of your library. On turn 6 you cast Excruciator, which leaves each player with only 6 cards in their library, and from there you close in about two turns:
- **Decking:** two Avaricies aimed at the opponent empty their library.
- **Damage:** with Bloodletter out, an Excruciator attack deals 12. Unholy Annex drains them for 4 at your end step once a Demon is on the board.

Archenemy's Charm exiles the blocker or answer in your way. If Excruciator gets removed, the Charm returns it to your hand so you can cast it again and shrink the libraries a second time.

1. **Dimir control with Excruciator as the finisher.** This is where Excruciator shows up in recent Dimir lists. I passed because two colors can't reliably make the BBB for the Charm and the BBBBBB for Excruciator.
2. **A pure "mill them out" deck** built on Excruciator plus Avarice. Its problem is your own library: after Excruciator you're down to 6 cards and drawing 2–3 a turn, so you'd deck yourself first.
3. **The Mono-Black shell from the format's results, which is what I chose.** It brings 24 lands with 23 black sources, plus Bloodletter, Unholy Annex and cheap removal. It's the strongest because Bloodletter makes Avarice a kill spell, not just a mill spell. Annex and Excruciator are both Demon cards, so they work together.

**Honest odds:**
- **Finding the plan:** you'll have Excruciator or an Avarice in hand by turn 6 about 81% of the time.
- **The full line:** the checker says you'll have drawn every card in the exact turn-7 line only about 4.5% of the time. That number doesn't count Avarice fetching Excruciator. Most games will be a midrange grind that gets there a turn or two later.
- **The danger:** once Excruciator resolves, your own 6-card library is a ticking clock. Only cast it when you can close within about two turns.

The sideboard is aimed at the green decks (Simic Ouroboroid, Landfall), Dimir and Jeskai control, and Reanimator.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Resonating Lute, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.
results.text:

- **Color:** It gives you black, so Inevitable Defeat ({1}{R}{W}{B}, uncounterable exile plus a 3-point life swing) costs just two lands.
- **Cost:** Jeskai Revelation (7 mana: bounce, 4 damage, two Monks, draw two, gain 4) can be cast off four lands, often with mana left over for a second spell the same turn.

Two Mystical Teachings work as extra copies. They find whichever Revelation or Defeat you need at instant speed, and their {5}{B} flashback is cheap with Lute out. The Monks, Helix burn and life drains close the game, with about turn 8 as the target. Since nearly every card is an instant or sorcery, Lute's own draw ability (when you hold seven or more cards) also comes up.

**The three directions I considered:**
1. **Jeskai Control plus black (chosen).** Real Inevitable Defeat decks already look like this. Lightning Helix, Get Lost, No More Lies and Consult show up in about 90% of the lists that run it, and Mystical Teachings in 56%.
2. **Izzet Lessons with Lute.** It has no white or black, so Revelation and Defeat would need a second splash.
3. **A big-spell Omniscience-style shell.** It takes the focus off your three cards.

I chose the first because it's the only one where Lute does two jobs: it doubles your mana and supplies the black for Defeat.

**Mana base:** 26 lands, which matches real Jeskai Control lists. The deck checker found no problems. There are 8 natural black sources: 3 Great Hall of the Biblioplex (any color for instants and sorceries), 2 Starting Town, and one each of Godless Shrine, Watery Grave and Blood Crypt. Lute covers black once it's down.

**Honest odds:** By turn 6 on the play, you'll draw a Lute about 60% of the time. That number doesn't count Consult, Stock Up or Three Steps Ahead, so the real chance is higher. The checker gave a 2.2% chance of drawing every card in the win line by turn 8, but that also ignores the tutors and card draw, and the deck doesn't need every piece to win.

The sideboard (Fire Magic and Pyroclasm against Prowess, Annul, Tishana's Tidebinder, Rest in Peace and others) is aimed at the decks that top the current field.

- **Call Forth the Tempest** cascades twice more, then deals damage to every enemy creature equal to the total mana value you've cast that turn. That's 15 or more if it comes off Creative Technique and Apex, which wipes out Tamiyo, Murktide Regent, Nadu and Ocelot Pride.

results.text:
I built **Grixis Buried Phoenix**, a brew. No published list has played these three cards together, so this is a new build.

**The plan:** Arclight Phoenix comes back from your graveyard at the start of combat if you've cast three or more instants or sorceries that turn. Buried Alive (a sorcery) puts three Phoenixes in your graveyard, and in this deck it's also the second of those three spells. The basic line is Dark Ritual → Buried Alive → Gut Shot paid with 2 life. That brings back three hasty 3/2 fliers for 9 damage as early as turn 1. Next turn, three more cheap spells finish the game, and they bring the Phoenixes back again if they get removed. Flow State is the refuel: with Dark Ritual (an instant) and Buried Alive (a sorcery) already in your graveyard, it puts two of the top three cards into your hand. That keeps the next turn's chain going.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Grixis ritual combo (chosen):** Dark Ritual and Lotus Petal speed out Buried Alive, and cheap or free spells reach the three-spell count. It's the fastest way to use Buried Alive.
2. **Izzet Tempo shell (from the menu) splashing Buried Alive:** Force of Will, Daze and cantrips. Those decks spend their mana on interaction, though, and black would only be a splash for the key card.
3. **Looting and discard, like Pioneer/Modern Phoenix:** proven, but slower. It leaves Buried Alive as just another discard outlet.

I chose the first because Dark Ritual is itself an instant. It counts toward the Phoenix trigger and puts an instant in the graveyard for Flow State, so all three requested cards help each other.

**What I borrowed and why:**
- **Interaction:** Force of Will, Brainstorm and Ponder, from the menu's tempo decks.
- **Free spells:** Entomb and Gitaxian Probe are banned in Legacy. Gut Shot (castable for 2 life) and Lava Dart's flashback (sacrifice a Mountain) are the free ways to get extra spells in a turn.
- **Lands:** 16. That's fewer than Izzet Tempo's usual 19, because 4 Lotus Petal and 4 Dark Ritual add mana. Every fetch land can find all three dual lands, and Volcanic Island and Badlands count as Mountains for Lava Dart.

**Honest odds:**
- Without counting cards your cantrips dig to, you see Buried Alive by turn 2 about 44.5% of the time, and by turn 3 about 49%.
- Brainstorm, Ponder and Flow State push that higher.
- Faithless Looting also puts any Phoenix you draw into the graveyard.
- The checker's 0.6% figure means drawing every card in the listed line. That includes Flow State, which is only an alternative third spell, so it understates the real chance.

**Weak points:** Graveyard hate like Surgical Extraction is a problem, and so are Orcish Bowmasters pings, since Phoenix has only 2 toughness.

The 15-card sideboard is aimed at the tempo decks and combo decks in the current field.

results.prompt: Brew me a Vintage deck built around Goblin Welder, Legion Extruder and Sewer-veillance Cam.
results.text:
I've built **UR "Sewer Welder"**, a brew for Vintage that takes its shell from Legacy's Sewer Combo deck. When I searched for decks running all three of your cards, the only two hits were both that Legacy list.

**How it wins:** Put Sewer-veillance Cam on the battlefield and Legion Extruder in the graveyard, then tap Goblin Welder to swap them.
1. Cam leaving the battlefield untaps Welder, and Extruder entering deals 2 damage to your opponent.
2. Tap Welder again to swap Extruder back out for Cam. Cam entering untaps Welder.
3. Repeat as often as you like. The loop costs no mana, so it's unlimited damage.

**Getting the pieces in place:**
- **Getting Extruder into the graveyard:** Goblin Engineer puts it there from your library. Melded Moxite's "discard a card, draw two" can bin one you've drawn.
- **Haste:** Welder can't tap the turn it comes in, so it normally goes off a turn later. Skateboard or Lavaspur Boots let it tap right away, and Urza's Saga can fetch either one.
- **Backup Welder:** Agatha's Soul Cauldron can exile a dead Welder and give its ability to Engineer.
- **Second win:** Painter's Servant plus Grindstone mills the opponent's whole library. Painter also lets Pyroblast hit any spell or permanent.

**Interaction:** 4 Pyroblast and 1 Red Elemental Blast in the main deck, since most of the top decks are blue.

**Directions I considered:**
- **Raker Shops prison shell** (Workshop, Grim Monolith, Sphere effects) with the loop as the finisher.
- **UR blue tempo** with Force of Will, Ancestral Recall and Time Walk.
- **The Legacy Sewer Combo port, boosted with Vintage fast mana.** I chose this one: it's the only proven home for all three cards, and Power plus Mishra's Workshop make it faster.

**Choices you might question:**
- **No Force of Will:** the deck has too few blue cards to pitch to it. The red blasts do that job, and the main deck still has Ancestral and Time Walk.
- **Melded Moxite:** the checker flagged it as rarely played in Vintage. I kept it because binning a combo piece from your hand is its job here.
- **Mana:** 15 lands plus 11 fast-mana artifacts, which matches how many lands the 150 Paradoxical Outcome lists in recent results play.

**Honest odds:** About 64% of the time (no mulligans), you'll have Welder or Engineer plus a combo piece or Moxite by turn 3. Having every card in the line drawn by turn 3 is rare (about 2%). The deck relies on Engineer, Moxite and Saga to find the rest, which that figure doesn't count, so expect the loop on turn 2–4 rather than a sure turn 3.

The 15-card sideboard is aimed at the decks in your meta snapshot: Lurrus/Paradoxical Outcome, Shops, Dredge and Initiative.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Ardent Recruit, Search Party Captain and Springleaf Drum.
results.text:
I built a Boros (red-white) artifact aggro deck around your three cards, using the support cards from the Boros Synthesizer deck in the current meta. No published list runs all three cards together, so this is an untested brew.

**The plan:** Play cheap creatures and artifacts in the first two turns, then attack with all of them.
- **Ardent Recruit:** a 3/3 for one white mana once you have three artifacts. The artifact sources are 24 cards:
  - 8 artifact lands
  - 4 Springleaf Drum
  - 3 Ornithopter
  - 4 Experimental Synthesizer
  - 1 Relic of Progenitus
  - 4 Thraben Inspector, which makes Clue artifacts
- **Search Party Captain:** costs 1 less for each creature that attacked this turn. Attack with three creatures and it costs one white mana, and it draws a card when it enters.
- **Springleaf Drum:** its cost taps a creature without the tap symbol, so a creature you just cast can pay it. Drum plus a free Ornithopter gives you extra mana of either color on turn 1. Glint Hawk and Kor Skyfisher can return Drum to your hand so you can recast it for 1.

Lightning Bolt and Galvanic Blast (4 damage once you have three artifacts) clear blockers or finish the opponent.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Mono-white Battle Screech:** many bodies for Captain, but too few artifacts for Recruit.
2. **Black-white Glintblade:** good removal, but no red burn to go with the artifact theme.
3. **Boros Synthesizer support cards (my choice):** Galvanic Blast gets stronger with the same artifacts Recruit needs. Glint Hawk and Kor Skyfisher already return cheap artifacts like Drum.

**Honest odds and caveats:**
- **Turn 4 odds:** you'll have Drum or Captain by turn 4 about 53% of the time each.
- **The sample win line is rare:** drawing every card in it by turn 5 happens only 0.2% of the time, so read it as an example. The deck wins by having lots of cheap creatures, not one exact sequence.
- **Lands:** I run 18, below the Synthesizer average of about 20.5. The average spell costs 1.36 and Drum makes extra mana. If you get mana-screwed, cut an Ornithopter for a land.
- **Relic of Progenitus:** I kept it over the more popular Nihil Spellbomb, whose card draw needs black mana. Relic also counts as an artifact and hurts the two biggest decks in the field, Tolarian Terror and Madness.

The 15-card sideboard covers the main matchups:
- 4 Red Elemental Blast against blue decks (Terror, Faeries)
- 3 Dust to Dust against Affinity and Golgari Gardens
- 2 Destroy Evil against big creatures
- 2 Prismatic Strands against Madness
- 2 Electrickery against Elves and white token decks
- 2 more Relic of Progenitus for graveyard decks

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Aurora Eidolon, Sandstorm Eidolon and Spirit Mascot.
results.text:
I built a Boros (red-white) deck where nearly every spell is multicolored. It's a brew: no published list has played these three cards together. It uses the mana base and the Faithless Looting / Thrilling Discovery discard cards from the Boros Aggro lists.

**How it works:** The Eidolons are mostly cards you throw away on purpose. Faithless Looting, Thrilling Discovery and Pumpkin Bombardment put them in the graveyard. Then any multicolored spell you cast returns each Eidolon to your hand, and each card leaving the graveyard puts a +1/+1 counter on Spirit Mascot.

- **Pumpkin Bombardment is the key card.** It counts as multicolored because its cost is black-or-red hybrid, and its discard is part of the cost. The Eidolon you discard is already in the graveyard when the spell is cast, so it comes straight back. You get 3 damage of removal for 1 mana without losing a card, and Mascot grows.
- **The deck has 28 multicolored spells.** Gold and hybrid cards like Boros Recruit, Feisty Spikeling, Wojek Halberdiers, Burning-Tree Emissary and Skyknight Legionnaire all trigger the Eidolons.
- **How you win:** Mascot gets bigger with every return. To finish, pay {R} and sacrifice Sandstorm Eidolon so their best blocker can't block. Pay {W} and sacrifice Aurora Eidolon to stop 3 damage aimed at Mascot. Both come back on your next multicolored spell, so you can do it again.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Boros multicolored aggro with the Boros Aggro discard cards (chosen).** It's the only direction that turns the Eidolons' "return on multicolored spell" text into a real engine. Pumpkin Bombardment, Thrilling Discovery and plenty of cheap hybrid creatures fuel it.
2. **The Synthesizer list with Kor Skyfisher.** Bouncing your own permanents does nothing for cards that come back from the graveyard.
3. **A three-color deck adding off-color hybrid cards like Abandon Attachments.** It made the mana worse and didn't add more triggers than staying in two colors.

**Odds and caveats:**
- By turn 4 you'll have a discard card 89% of the time, an Eidolon 68% and Spirit Mascot 53%. All three together is about 30%.
- The checker gave my exact turn-6 sequence 0.5%, but that line needs specific named cards. Any hybrid spell works in place of the named ones, so it isn't the real chance of the plan coming together.
- Even without the full engine, the deck plays as a low-curve aggro deck with Lightning Bolt.
- The Eidolons run 3 copies each. One copy in the graveyard keeps coming back, so more would clog your hand.
- The deck has 12 white sources against about 16 in real Boros Aggro lists. That's on purpose: this deck leans red (Bolt, Looting, Bombardment, Emissary), and most white costs are hybrid.

The 15-card sideboard is aimed at the current top decks:
- Red Elemental Blast and Pyroblast for Terror
- Dust to Dust for Affinity
- Electrickery for Elves and Mono-White
- Prismatic Strands, Journey to Nowhere and Thraben Charm

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Living Death.
results.text:
I built a black-green Living Death deck. It uses the mana and discard spells of BG Survival, the deck where Living Death shows up most in recent Premodern results (3 of its 7 recent lists).

**The directions I considered:**
1. **The BG Survival build (chosen).** Fill the graveyard with Survival of the Fittest, Buried Alive and Krosan Tusker, then Living Death brings back a whole board of big creatures.
2. **A fast mono-black build.** Dark Ritual into Buried Alive, then Living Death. It's faster, but the creatures it brings back are weaker, and it has fewer ways to fill the graveyard.
3. **A Hermit Druid build.** Hermit Druid mills most of the deck, then Living Death brings it all back. But the proven Druid combo lists run almost no basic lands and win in other ways. Druid would also mill your own copies of Living Death.

I picked the first one because Survival does two jobs at once. Each time you use it, it puts a creature in your graveyard and finds the next one. That gives Living Death the best targets and keeps the deck playable when you haven't drawn it.

**The plan:** Turn 1 Birds of Paradise, turn 2 Survival. From turn 3, Survival discards creatures to find more creatures. Krosan Tusker can also discard itself through cycling, and Buried Alive puts three creatures in the graveyard at once. On turn 4–5, Living Death makes the opponent sacrifice their board and returns your stocked graveyard:
- **Deranged Hermit** makes four 2/2 Squirrels.
- **Penumbra Wurm** is a 6/6 that leaves another 6/6 if it dies.
- **Bone Shredder** kills whatever creature the opponent got back.
- **Krosan Tusker and Ravenous Baloth** add big bodies.

Living Death affects both players, so Withered Wretch is there to remove the opponent's best creatures from their graveyard first. Duress and Cabal Therapy clear counterspells out of the way; Stiflenought, the most played deck right now at 15% of the field, plays a lot of them. Avatar of Woe often costs only two black mana here, because it gets 6 cheaper once there are ten creature cards across all graveyards.

**How reliable it is:**
- You see Living Death by turn 5 on the play about 57% of the time.
- You see Living Death plus at least one of the 10 graveyard-filling cards about 50% of the time.
- Most of the creatures are 1–3 copies because Survival and Buried Alive find them. That's why the checker reported a 0% chance of naturally drawing every card in the exact win line. It doesn't count tutors, so ignore that number.

**The mana:** 22 lands plus 4 Birds of Paradise, giving 15 black sources and 17 green. This is in line with real BG Survival lists.

**The sideboard** targets the current field:
- **Engineered Plague:** Goblins and Elves
- **Naturalize:** Enchantress, Oath and Sulfuric Vortex
- **Tormod's Crypt and a second Withered Wretch:** Replenish and Reanimator
- **Xantid Swarm:** counterspell decks
- **Smother and Pernicious Deed:** creature decks
